There was a low jingle, a glint of yellow metal, a sway of fringed draperies, and she
stopped as if her heart had failed her. The young fellow by my side growled. The pilgrims
murmured at my back. She looked at us all as if her life had depended upon the unswerving
steadiness of her glance. Suddenly she opened her bare arms and threw them up rigid above
her head, as though in an uncontrollable desire to touch the sky, and at the same time the
swift shadows darted out on the earth, swept around on the river, gathering the steamer
into a shadowy embrace. A formidable silence hung over the scene.
